implementation_summary: New module assessment.ts. assessPages(input, ai: AuditAiResolution) makes one 'assessment' stage request per Sample Page, in sequence. The request carries a size-capped JSON summary of the page: title, headings, Sections, CTAs, ranked findings (id, area, title, impact, effort, sectionId), area grades ('not checked' when null) and PageSpeed lab/field values or the reason they were not measured. assessSite does the same once with the url, the Sample Pages and every finding of the audit. The prompt asks for {areas:[{area,note,evidence}]} for all six AUDIT_AREAS, written in the audit's document language (DOCUMENT_LANGUAGE_INFO name), with no grades or scores and none of the ADR 0018 words. Page data is marked as data only. The output grade always comes from the caller's grades (?? null). Only note (trimmed, max 1200 characters) and evidence are read from the answer. Evidence is filtered to ids in the input findings and de-duplicated. An unparsable answer gets one repair request. Missing notes and notes with claim words (findClaimWords) get one combined repair request; areas still bad become not-done ai-failed. No key gives every area no-ai-key. A provider error or AITimeoutError gives ai-failed with no error text kept. Budget spent gives budget-spent. A cancel from the caller is re-thrown as AbortError.
tests_proposed: Runner integration test: an audit run fills AuditPage.areas and AuditResult.siteAreas from assessPages/assessSite and adds the no-key note to AuditResult.notes.

risks: assessment.ts imports parseJsonAnswer from packages/core/src/plan/ai-planner.ts, so the audit module now depends on the planner module.
A page can take up to 3 AI requests (answer, parse repair, claim/missing repair); budget planning should allow for this.
If the repair request fails or the budget runs out on it, only the areas being repaired become not-done; clean notes from the first answer are kept.

Page text sent to the AI is capped (40 headings, 40 sections, 25 CTAs, 60 findings, 200 characters per field). The prompt marks page data as data only, but prompt injection is not fully preventable; the output is limited by the claim-word check and the evidence-id filter.
The claim-word check uses the full ADR 0018 list plus the release-verdict words from findClaimWords, wider than the five words in the acceptance criterion.
handoff: Runner: resolution = await resolveAuditAi({...}); pageAreas = await assessPages({language: result.language, pages: samplePages.map(p => ({urlPath, content: PageContent, findings: that page's ranked findings, grades: AreaGrades, speed})), signal, timeoutMs}, resolution) -> PageAssessment[] {urlPath, areas}; siteAreas = await assessSite({language, url, pages: [{urlPath, title, speed?}], findings: all audit findings, grades, signal}, resolution) -> AreaAssessment[]. Areas are always the six AUDIT_AREAS in order. A cancel from the caller rejects with AbortError. When the reason is 'no-ai-key', add the tool-user note 'AI notes need an AI key.' Exports: assessPages, assessSite, AreaGrades, AssessmentPageInput, AssessPagesInput, AssessSiteInput, AssessmentRunOptions, PageAssessment.
